IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Wednesday, September 16, 2026**

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** is moving volume—61 calls, ~420 hands on the board. Miller Electrical, Inglett & Stubbs, and Whitehead Electric are all hunting at **$42/hr** for inside JW work across QTS data centers and feeder pulls in Fayetteville. Inglett & Stubbs is running 4-10's and 2-8's Monday through Saturday, so if you're chasing steady hours, that's your play. Book depth is solid but not screaming desperation yet.

**LU-494 Milwaukee, WI** is the standout right now—43 calls, only ~207 hands. Cupertino and Gurtz both need 30 JW's each at the Port Washington Data Center running **$10/hr over scale** plus a Wisconsin license. These are 58-60 hour weeks; pure volume work. Cupertino wants that OT punch, Gurtz wants 60 flat. Tight board, fat hours.

**LU-26 Washington, DC** has 64 calls across data center work (Sterling, Ashburn) with JE Richards and Hanley Energy—no hourly posted, but book depth suggests availability. Specified's flagging fire alarm techs needing NICET F/A Systems level 2; Mass is doing WMATA traction power. Solid infrastructure play if you're east-coast bound.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** is the sleeper. Parsons Electric has 30 and 20 JW calls at the Polaris Forge Data Center in Harwood running **$44.80/hr** plus **$100/day non-taxed per diem** weekdays, **$150/day Saturday-Sunday, 6-10 schedules**. That's real money in the Midwest—50 hands needed, light board. North Dakota license not required on the first call; drug test and two forms of ID.

**LU-575 Portsmouth, OH** just opened Monday, September 21: TSG's got 97 journeymen needed at Amazon North Campus, Jeffersonville, running 4-10's. Blattner's Palomino Solar Field (Hillsboro) needs 9 more on 5-8 schedules same start date. Both projects kick off this week.

**LU-354 Salt Lake City, UT** is Cache Valley Electric at Proctor & Gamble Corrine, **$46.22/hr**, 6-10's possibly stretching to 6-12's—25 calls, book barely breathing at ~130 hands.

Data center work and solar construction are eating the board nationally right now; Milwaukee's premium overscale and Grand Forks' per diem structure are magnets for traveling hands.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Tuesday, September 15, 2026**

**LU-71 Columbus, OH** is the board to watch right now—46 calls across the state with NEW RIVER ELECT. CORP. running the show. Forty journeymen headed to Columbus proper on 6-10s, $125/night per diem plus a $125 bonus on 10-hour days, all distribution work requiring CDL. Nine more going south on 4-10s (optional Fri/Sat) at the same diem. Book depth is solid at ~140 hands, which means you've got real shot at movement.

**LU-70 Forestville, MD** is running 14 calls on a tight board (~32 hands), but the money is *there*. Miller Bros has a substation gig in the DC area paying **$126/hr** with **$125** per diem—that's the top single call on the entire board today. LE Myers is pushing transmission work out of Culpeper at **$55** plus **$150** diem; Thayer's running shenandoah Valley distribution at **$71/hr** with **$125** diem and a **$150** bonus at 55 hours. All CDL A, all solid.

**LU-1393 Indianapolis, IN** has 39 calls across 65 hands. Kent Power's pulling a transmission 345KV bundle rebuild out of Gary at **$67.18/hr**—highest single call in the midwest block—with **$150/day** per diem. ARC American's running 12.5K rebuilds in Wanatah at **$64.66** with CDL A requirement.

**LU-84 Newnan, GA** is 36 calls deep on 127 hands. SERVICE ELECTRIC's barehand certification work in Social Circle hits **$56.80/hr** (**$10/hr** over the base rate) plus **$150/day**, Georgia Transmission line work. Faith Electric's college park jobs start at **$49.80** with **$150/day** and hotels covered—hotels, not diem.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** sits at 25 calls (87 hands) with Parsons Electric's Polaris Forge data center pull: 30 Inside JW at **$44.80/hr**, **$100/day** nontaxable diem (100+ miles) on 6-10s with a **$100** Mon-Fri and **$150** Sat/Sun incentive. Heavy industrial backbone driving demand.

The work is chasing data centers and transmission backbone—Harwood, Amarillo, the midwest industrial corridor. Skill-certified work (barehand, nuclear, transmission) is commanding premiums. Boards are moving.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Tuesday, September 15, 2026**

**LU-290 Portland, OR** is running the board heavy at 23 calls chasing 47 hands. Intel Ronler Acres in Hillsboro is the spine here—Apollo Mechanical wants 8 CAD/BIM detailers, Charter's got 5 fitters and 4 high-purity crews, plus 3 orbital welders all on tool install work. Book depth is real; this is sustained semiconductor fab work and you're not walking in cold.

**LU-140 Salt Lake City, UT** sits fat with 18 calls and 61 hands needed. BCS Mechanical dominates the Sego Project in West Valley—15 journeyman pipefitters, 13 journeyman plumbers, 5 apprentices all running 4-10s starting August 3. DSI's QTS data center gig in Eagle Mountain adds 6 more pipefitters on **$10.00** (night shift, 5-10s + 1-8). This is volume work; Sego alone could absorb most of Book 1.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** is tight and specialty. Kiewit's offering **$65** for a CWI inspector position with 5-10s plus Saturday nights, night shift premium bumping it 15%. US Eng. Metalworks needs fitters with stainless experience on shop night work; Broadcom in Fort Collins wants high-purity tube benders. High skill floor, solid depth at 13 calls.

**LU-776 Lima, OH** is small but industrial-heavy—5 calls, 26 hands. Cenovus maintenance runs the show with pipefitters and combo welders across Gem's fab shop (6-10s) and Nooter's fab operation (**PD $125/day**). Graham's got steady maintenance work; Upland's Lima Data Center gig pays all OT at double time on 5-10s and 8s.

**LU-213 St. John, NB** shows refinery and pulp-and-paper traction. Irving Oil Refinery needs F3/F4 welders (days and night shifts via CAM and Stuart Olson), plus apprentice instrument techs. Irving Pulp and Paper is calling for a journeyman pipefitter nights on 4-10s. Canadian work, but industrial process piping sustains these boards.

Semiconductor fabs and data centers are pulling hands out of regional books faster than traditional industrial work—specialty certifications and clean-room experience are the gates now.
